verifications.claim: Active auroral conditions (Kp 4) are forecasted for mid-March 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R8: 'NOAA is predicting a Kp index of four out of nine on Saturday night'; R1: 'Kp = 4' shown as moderate/active levels; R5: 'moderate (G2) storm level' (G2=Kp6)
verifications.reasoning: R8 directly supports Kp4 for mid-March weekend; R1 associates Kp4 with active/moderate aurora; R5 implies higher G2 (Kp6), but claim specifies Kp4 in broader terms.

verifications.claim: Potential visibility of aurora in northern U.S. states and high-latitude regions is forecasted for mid-March 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'northern lights could be visible across parts of the northern United States this weekend... northern parts of Washington, Idaho, Montana...'; R8: 'aurora borealis could be spotted Saturday in Alaska, northern Washington... northern Maine'
verifications.reasoning: Both R5 and R8 explicitly forecast aurora visibility in northern U.S. states for mid-March 2026 weekend.

verifications.claim: A G1 (Minor) storm is possible due to solar winds.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R8: 'geomagnetic storm that was upgraded from minor to moderate levels'; R5: 'fast-moving stream of solar wind... triggered geomagnetic storm conditions... moderate (G2)'
verifications.reasoning: R8 mentions minor (G1) as initial/possible before upgrade; R5 attributes to solar wind but reports G2; supports possibility vaguely.

verifications.claim: A G1 (Minor) storm would make the northern lights visible low on the horizon as far south as parts of the US northern tier.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'moderate displays may be visible... low on the horizon as far south as Bethel...'; R5: 'low on the northern horizon... northern US states'; R8: similar northern states visibility
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe low-horizon visibility in northern U.S. tier during minor/moderate storms (G1~Kp5 aligns with Kp4 descriptions).

verifications.claim: Forecasted aurora visibility area for March 15-16, 2026 includes Northern US (WA, MT, ND, MN, WI, MI, ME), Alaska, Canada, and Northern Europe.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R5: 'through Monday, March 16... Alaska... northern Washington, Idaho, Montana, North Dakota... Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, and Maine'; R8: 'Saturday... Alaska, northern Washington... Montana, North Dakota... Minnesota... northern Michigan and northern Maine'
verifications.reasoning: Exact states mostly match (minor extras like ID/SD); dates align with March 15-16; Canada/N. Europe implied as high-latitude but not explicitly listed.

verifications.claim: Forecasted aurora intensity for March 15-16, 2026 is Active (Kp 4).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R8: 'Kp index of four out of nine on Saturday night... slightly less on Sunday—at three'; R5: 'G2-level storm' for period through March 16
verifications.reasoning: R8 supports Kp4 (active) for Saturday/Sunday near dates; R5 higher G2; specific dates/dates close but intensity broadly active.

verifications.claim: Highest auroral activity is typically in late evening (10 PM to 2 AM local time).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'best time... three or four hours centered around midnight... 9 p.m. to 3 a.m.'; R8: 'best time to view... typically between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m.'
verifications.reasoning: Both sources directly state peak activity around late evening/midnight local time.

verifications.claim: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center offers a 30-minute forecast to see the currently forecasted auroral oval.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: '30 to 90 minute forecast of the location and intensity of the aurora... green oval'; R2: 'estimates what the next 30 minutes will be like... auroral oval'
verifications.reasoning: R4 and R2 explicitly describe NOAA's 30-minute aurora forecast showing oval.

verifications.claim: Geophysical Institute at UAF offers localized forecasts, particularly for Alaska.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Aurora Forecast | Geophysical Institute (https://www.gi.alaska.edu...)... Alaska Forecast: Moderate aurora activity forecasted... overhead from Utqiaġvik to...'
verifications.reasoning: R1 is the exact site from Geophysical Institute (UAF/Alaska) providing Alaska-specific forecasts.
